review_notes: I read the whole file. It has no simp lemmas or attributes, so I looked only at the rewrite interface used by its proof. That meant reading spectralL2ComplexMultiplier_pairing_test and the *_smooth_ae lemmas in SpectralWeightedPairing.lean. I also compared the same local rewrite lemmas in SpectralChainBoundaryBalance.lean, where they appear twice. I did not find a loop, competing rule or unwanted expansion. The only concern is a missing reusable rewrite lemma. Whether it should also be @[simp] is uncertain. Nothing was compiled, so the proposed lemma names and orientations are untested.

findings.problem: The proof rewrites with two local lemmas, `hv` and `hd`. Each turns `inner ℂ (spectralHarmonicValue/Derivative … (spectralHarmonicSmoothEmbedding ell R f)) (spectralRadialWeightMultiplier R w v)` into the explicit weighted integral. They are proved only by an eight-underscore application of `spectralL2ComplexMultiplier_pairing_test` and are not exposed as named lemmas. The same two `have`s are copied verbatim twice in SpectralChainBoundaryBalance.lean. There is no canonical rewrite rule for this normal form, so every use site rebuilds it and then drives it with `rw [hv, hv, hd, …]`, or with `rw [hv (…)] at h` in the other file. The rewrite is quantified over `v`, so `rw` can only match it in a fixed order.
findings.proposed_change: Add two named lemmas in SpectralWeightedPairing.lean, next to the *_smooth_ae lemmas. One would be `spectralHarmonicValue_smooth_inner_weightMultiplier` and the other `spectralHarmonicDerivative_smooth_inner_weightMultiplier`. Each states the current `hv`/`hd` equation for general `w`/`a`, with the inner product on the left and the integral on the right. Consider marking them `@[simp]`. The left side is a specific inner product that the right side does not reproduce, so there is no cycle risk. The right-hand integral contains no `inner`, so it is a smaller normal form. Then this proof can use `rw [spectralHarmonicValue_smooth_inner_weightMultiplier, …]` or `simp only [...]`. The duplicated blocks in SpectralChainBoundaryBalance.lean can use the same lemmas.
findings.benefit: The pairing-to-integral rewrite is stated once and has a discoverable name. Later flux-balance proofs can use it without restating it. Rewriting no longer depends on the order of `rw [hv, hv, hd, …]`.
